variants.headline: Looking back: assembly votes down government bill
variants.sub: The Assembly has rejected a bill put forward by the government.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A government bill had been voted down in the Colonial Assembly.

A legislature is supposed to decide, not merely to decorate a government's intentions. Our principles require us to take a rejected measure seriously without assuming that every rejection is wise. The merits of a political proposal belong in the argument; possession of office cannot settle them on its own.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The conduct of {target} warrants examination against the rejected proposal. This paper records the legislative result without adopting an unreported explanation for it or declaring a wider political outcome.

variants.headline: Looking back: a proposal meets its parliamentary limit
variants.sub: A proposed government bill has failed in the Assembly vote.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The Assembly had rejected a bill put forward by the government.

A legislature is supposed to decide, not merely to decorate a government's intentions. Our principles require us to take a rejected measure seriously without assuming that every rejection is wise. The merits of a political proposal belong in the argument; possession of office cannot settle them on its own.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

variants.headline: Looking back: government legislation fails the vote
variants.sub: A government bill has been voted down in the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:

The merits of a political proposal belong in the argument; possession of office cannot settle them on its own.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.
